extracted.intended_audience: Investigators preparing or responding to NIH R01 renewal applications (biomedical/HIV prevention) and NIH peer reviewers
extracted.subtask_description: Summary Statement and peer-review criteria used to evaluate an NIH R01 renewal application, listing criterion scores, strengths/weaknesses, and administrative determinations (human subjects, budget, inclusion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Impact (Impact Score)
rubrics_metrics.description: Overall Impact: committee's assessment of the likelihood that the project will exert a sustained, powerful influence on the research field. Impact Score: calculated after discussion by averaging the overall scores (1-9) given by all voting reviewers on the committee and multiplying by 10.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion scores are submitted prior to the meeting by assigned reviewers and are not discussed specifically at the review meeting or calculated into the overall impact score. Reviewers' written critiques illustrate how strengths and weaknesses across criteria inform the overall impact judgment (examples of strengths/weaknesses provided in critiques). See http://grants.nih.gov/grants/peer_review_process.htm#scoring for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of whether the project addresses an important problem or a critical barrier to progress in the field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example strengths from critiques: 'Objective measures of adherence are needed'; aims study hair levels in multiple PrEP modalities; hair levels well suited for resource-limited areas; inclusion of both hair and serum levels allows triangulation. Example weaknesses: potential redundancy with recently/pending-published work (e.g., Aim 1 renal toxicity—how different from an in-press Lancet HIV paper). Reviewers list specific strengths/weaknesses to justify numeric criterion scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigator(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the investigators' qualifications, productivity, and ability to carry out the proposed work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example strengths: 'Excellent set of investigators', 'highly productive in prior funding period (20 papers)', strong integration with parent studies and necessary collaborations/letters of support. Example weaknesses: typically none noted in these critiques, but reviewers comment on clarity of roles and justification of personnel costs (e.g., unclear student role justification).

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of whether the application challenges and seeks to shift current research or clinical practice paradigms using novel concepts, approaches, or methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example strengths: use of hair levels to study cumulative drug exposure across new PrEP modalities (vaginal ring, long-acting injectables) considered innovative; coupling hair with plasma and other measures. Example weaknesses: using hair to examine adherence per se may be viewed as an incremental advance; segmental analysis is novel but underutilized in some aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the overall strategy, methodology, analyses, and whether they are well-reasoned and appropriate to accomplish the aims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strengths cited: robust sampling and analysis plans (e.g., estimated seroconverter/control sampling ratios), commitment from parent study PIs, integration into ongoing trials, planned segmental hair analyses for PK. Weaknesses cited: methods for 'patterns of adherence' analyses are underdeveloped and not adequately described; segmental analyses not yet piloted in the Gandhi lab; RPV concentrations not addressed; power analyses may assume large effect sizes and not leverage repeated measures. Reviewers expect clear analytic methods, pilot data for novel assays, and justification of power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of institutional support, equipment, and other physical resources available to the investigators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical guidance: strong institutional environment (e.g., UCSF and Hair Analytical Laboratory well-equipped) is a strength. Letters of support demonstrating feasibility and integration into parent trials strengthen this criterion. Weaknesses rarely noted when environment is excellent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protections for Human Subjects / Human Subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of risks to human subjects and adequacy of protections, including consent and confidentiality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determinations in this summary: 'Acceptable Risks and/or Adequate Protections' but reviewers noted the human subjects plan did not address data confidentiality explicitly; PI will likely receive identifiable data that must be protected. Reviewers expect explicit plans for confidentiality and data protection when identifiable information is accessed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data and Safety Monitoring Plan (DSMP)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of whether appropriate monitoring plans are in place for clinical trials or embedded evaluations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not applicable for applications with no clinical trials; where embedded in parent trials, reviewers check that a DSMP is in place for those trials (noted as 'Acceptable' in critiques).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of Women, Minorities and Children
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of plans to include both sexes/genders, racial/ethnic groups, and children when scientifically appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summary judgments here: distributions justified scientifically; inclusion/exclusion of children under 18 justified; reviewers may flag oddities in planned demographic coding or small subgroup sizes (e.g., comment that all Hispanics from ACTG planned as 'mixed race' seems unlikely). For NIH-defined Phase III trials, reviewers would assess plans for valid design and analysis (not applicable here).

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate Animals
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment whether vertebrate animals are involved and if applicable whether protections are adequate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not Applicable in this application; criterion still recorded and marked when not relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biohazards
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of biosafety issues and protections for potentially hazardous materials or procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not Applicable in this application; criterion still recorded and marked when not relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Renewal (Prior Productivity / Progress)
rubrics_metrics.description: For renewal applications: assessment of prior period productivity, accomplishment of original aims, and justification for continued funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example guidance: prior R01 produced 20 papers and completed most aims; one aim on-going due to parent protocol delays. Prior productivity and progress are strong positive factors for renewal decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource Sharing Plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of plans for sharing data, resources, or materials resulting from the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marked 'Not Applicable' in this case when no relevant resources; reviewers expect a plan when relevant resources will be generated and will note acceptability or absence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentication of Key Biological and/or Chemical Resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of plans to authenticate biological and chemical resources used in the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marked 'Not Applicable' when no relevant resources; where applicable, reviewers expect authentication plans to guard against reproducibility issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget and Period of Support / Committee Budget Recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of requested budget, period of support, potential overlaps, and justification of specific costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee may recommend budget as requested or suggest modifications; administrative note: if an award is planned, grants management staff will calculate final costs based on committee recommendations. Reviewers may flag weak justifications for specific personnel or costs (example: unclear role/justification for a student and associated cost).

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative/FOIA/Confidentiality Notes
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative guidance about release of application materials and protections under FOIA, and contact information for program office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text notes that application text is copyrighted, NIAID posts for educational purposes with restrictions, and FOIA responses will be redacted to protect confidential reviewer deliberations, commercial/financial information, and personal privacy. Contact info provided for NIAID Office of Knowledge and Educational Resources.
